cards.confidenceNote: Declaration text quoted by BBC and The Guardian (both read); outcome assessments are analysts' views.
cards.title: Trump, Xi and Putin issue joint declaration at first three-way summit
cards.summary: The three leaders met for about 90 minutes in Shenzhen on 19 November and issued a declaration that nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. It called for UN reform, more oil supply and limits on the International Criminal Court, and did not mention Ukraine or Iran.
cards.body:
The Shenzhen meeting was the first three-way session of US, Chinese and Russian leaders, held on the sidelines of APEC after separate Trump-Putin and Trump-Xi bilaterals the same day. Its written output is short. The nuclear sentence repeats the formula the five permanent Security Council members adopted in 2022, so it restates an existing commitment rather than creating a new one. There is no number, no verification step and no date for talks, and Xi used the occasion to repeat China's long-standing call for nuclear weapons to be prohibited over time, the argument Beijing uses to stay out of US-Russia style limits.

What the declaration includes says as much as what it leaves out. Oil supply and UN reform give each leader a deliverable at home; the clause on the International Criminal Court protects officials of all three states. The two wars the participants are fighting or backing, Ukraine and Iran, are absent. Kyiv and European capitals read that absence as a sign that great-power bargaining can proceed over their heads; Britain's opposition leader called the meeting disturbing and Zelensky said big powers cannot decide the world's fate.

The summit is engagement, not a change in posture: its content is declaratory. It does mean the nuclear-risk channel among the three now has a leaders' text to point to; whether officials follow it with talks is the testable next step.

The Russian side paired summitry with pressure: the next morning Russian cruise missiles crashed in Poland during one of the war's largest attacks, and earlier in the week Russian bombers flew to Vietnam. China, meanwhile, began licensing exports of drone engines Russia relies on, a narrow but real constraint that Kyiv welcomed while saying many components remain uncontrolled.

cards.confidenceNote: Plea, alert and listing read on Military Times, Breaking Defense, BBC and Al Jazeera pages; the ship-cyber probe rests on a WSJ report carried by gCaptain.
cards.title: US Army sergeant pleads guilty to passing HIMARS secrets to China
cards.summary: Army supply sergeant Jian Zhao pleaded guilty on 24 November to conspiring to pass defence information, including HIMARS material, to China-connected people. Britain warned defence firms of Russian proxy arson the same day. The US blacklisted Megaspeed on 23 November, and the WSJ reports a probe of suspected Iranian cyberattacks on up to 50 ships.
cards.body:
Four cases in three days show the technology contest running on several fronts at once, and each points at a different adversary.

The Zhao plea is the China file. A supply sergeant at Joint Base Lewis-McChord admitted conspiring from late 2021 to early 2025 to sell national defence information, including excerpts of HIMARS technical manuals, photographs of restricted briefings and government computers, to people connected to China; a co-conspirator had already pleaded guilty and sentencing is set for 1 March 2027. HIMARS is the long-range rocket system at the centre of US plans for Taiwan and the Philippines, so the target matters more than the sums involved, which were small.

The Megaspeed listing is the export-control file. On 23 November the Commerce Department added the Singapore data-centre firm at the centre of the Nvidia diversion affair, and six other Southeast Asian firms, to its Entity List; Singapore opened its own investigation. Beijing has not yet answered, and the board will watch whether it uses its own licensing tools on rare earths or drone parts in reply, as it did in October.

The Russia file is sabotage rather than theft. Britain's protective security agency, run by MI5, told defence firms and suppliers to Ukraine on 24 November that Russia has stepped up attempts to sabotage European defence sites, mainly through arson by low-level proxies hired online. It is a warning, not a new incident, but it formalises what Estonia, Germany and Denmark have attributed case by case, and it comes a week after the US charged a Russian with spying on Palantir staff in California.

The Iran file is the least certain. The Wall Street Journal reported on 23 November that US authorities are investigating suspected cyberattacks on as many as 50 tankers and chemical carriers, some sent bomb threats, with Iran the main suspect and Russia a possible one. No US agency has attributed the attacks on the record, and Reuters could not verify the report. If it holds, the Hormuz confrontation has a cyber front against commercial shipping alongside the drones and projectiles UKMTO logs.

What would change the picture: a named US attribution of the ship attacks; a Chinese counter-listing after Megaspeed; or a first sabotage incident in Britain tied to the proxies the alert describes.

cards.confidenceNote: Bahrain and UKMTO statements read via Al Jazeera, Euronews and gCaptain; Iranian claims are statements of record only; no US confirmation of strikes in the window.
cards.title: Iran hits Bahrain civilian site as tanker attacks near Khasab rise
cards.summary: Bahrain said an Iranian attack set fire to a civilian industrial facility on 21 November, with no injuries. UKMTO logged three tanker-attack reports near Khasab on 20-21 November, without casualties. Iran's Guard said it struck US Patriot radars and claimed two US drones; the US did not confirm any strike on Iran in the window.
cards.body:
The exchange that resumed on 17 November with the US strike on Qeshm has settled into Iranian pressure on two fronts: Gulf states hosting US forces, and shipping in the strait. Bahrain has now reported Iranian attacks repeatedly since 13 November; the 21 November raid is the first in this round to cause reported damage at a civilian site, a fire at an unnamed industrial facility, with no injuries. The Guard's own account says it targeted Patriot radars at two bases in response to US drone flights over Iran and an attack on a radar on Hengam Island. No US statement on Hengam has been found, and explosions reported at Sirik after the Bahrain raid are unattributed.

At sea, UKMTO reported a tanker hit near Khasab on 20 November and two more attack reports near Khasab on 21 November, which may have involved the same vessel; none caused casualties. Iran's navy says a tanker hit a mine in a restricted zone east of the strait, which Reuters could not verify. Al Jazeera's Tehran correspondent, citing Iranian armed-forces statements, counted about 25 incidents in a week. Iran's message is that passage requires its coordination; the US answer remains the blockade, extended on 18 November to ship-to-ship transfers.

Washington has not struck back on Iranian soil in the window. Trump said he is not rushing a decision, and Qatari mediators visited Tehran on 20 November. That keeps the kinetic picture inside the band this board already scores: sustained state-on-state fire under a blockade, without a widening US campaign. The next markers are a US strike answering Bahrain, any casualties in a Gulf state, and whether Iranian tankers try to run the blockade from Kharg.

Iraq removed one variable: its forces entered Kataib Hezbollah's Jurf al-Sakhar base on 20 November under a compromise, reducing the risk of an Iraqi front opening against US interests.

cards.confidenceNote: Trump remarks read via Iran International (Fox interview); Qatar statement via BBC and NYT.
cards.title: Trump calls the Islamabad deal 'a waste of time' as talks stall
cards.summary: Trump told Fox News the preliminary Islamabad understanding had been 'a waste of time' and said he would finish the war 'one way or the other.' Qatar, the mediator, called Iran's attacks on Kuwait and Bahrain a dangerous escalation. Trump said he would not ask Xi or Putin for help on Iran.
cards.body:
The diplomatic track is now a holding pattern with the US openly discounting it. Trump told Fox News that the preliminary understanding reached in Islamabad had been 'a waste of time,' useful only for assessing Tehran's approach, and that he wanted a lasting deal and would 'finish it off — soon. One way or the other.' He said he would not ask Xi or Putin for help because the US had defeated Iran's navy and air force and controlled the Strait. On 12 November he had told the Vice-President to drop the talks.

The mediators have not walked away. Qatar condemned Iran's attacks on its neighbours as a dangerous escalation that complicates efforts to contain tensions, and an Emirati official told the Manama Dialogue that the UAE does not believe a military solution is viable. The New York Times reports that Iran's leaders hardened their position after Trump's midterm losses, according to American, European and Iranian officials.

Two threat claims widen the gap. CNN reported, citing US officials, that Iran was preparing plans for a dirty bomb or chemical attack on senior US officials in Washington; the White House said there were no credible threats to the homeland, and Trump said Iran was 'looking at gas, looking at bio.' Neither claim has a government document behind it on the pages read.

What would move this card: a dated round of talks with both parties present, a Qatari or Omani text, or an Iranian offer that drops the two-day reopening conditions.

cards.confidenceNote: Gaza incursion read on NYT and France 24; joint strike planning is one NYT report citing officials.
cards.title: Israeli tanks cross Gaza ceasefire line as joint Iran strike plans reported
cards.summary: Israeli tanks crossed Gaza's ceasefire line on 18 November in the first armoured incursion since the truce, displacing 5,200 people. Israel killed Hamas's Rafah brigade commander on 14 November. US and Israeli officials have drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran, the New York Times reported.
cards.body:
Two Israeli moves in one week point the same way. On 18 November the military sent tanks and engineering machinery across the ceasefire line into Hamas-held central Gaza, calling it a limited raid on infrastructure that threatened its forces; the New York Times describes it as the first time heavy armour has gone far across that line since the truce. Hamas called it a blatant violation, and Gaza's civil defence said 5,200 people were displaced. Four days earlier a drone strike killed Rafah brigade commander Samir Abu Younis in al-Mawasi, which Hamas confirmed. Gaza's health ministry counts more than 1,600 people killed by Israeli fire during the ceasefire.

On Iran, the New York Times reports that American and Israeli military officials have drawn up plans for renewed strikes, most likely on energy infrastructure, with no decision taken. That is the relationship's operational core: planning together while the US President says he will finish the war one way or the other.

At home, Netanyahu remains caretaker while Gadi Eisenkot holds the mandate to form a government; Netanyahu keeps authority over the Gaza, Lebanon and Iran fronts in the meantime.

The tension to watch is Washington's own plan: the US-brokered Gaza framework rests on staged Israeli withdrawal, and an armoured raid outside the line tests whether Washington objects in public, as it did over Lebanon in August, or lets it pass.

cards.confidenceNote: Facts read on BBC, Guardian, Al Jazeera pages; scenario weights are the board's judgement.
cards.title: Russian missiles hit Poland a day after the Shenzhen nuclear declaration
cards.summary: Trump, Xi and Putin declared on 19 November that nuclear war must never be fought. On 20 November Russian cruise missiles crashed in Poland during a mass attack on Ukraine, and on 21 November Iran struck Bahrain and tankers near Hormuz. The board's score holds at 66.
cards.body:
The window shows the distance between leaders' declarations and the two wars. The Shenzhen text was the most significant joint statement by the three nuclear powers this year, yet it ignored Ukraine and Iran, and within a day each war produced a fresh escalation step outside its main theatre: Russian missiles inside NATO territory, Iranian fire causing damage at a civilian site in Bahrain.

Both steps sit inside the bands the board already scores. Poland reported no injuries; NATO scrambled jets but did not engage; Warsaw is asking for more air defence rather than invoking collective defence. In the Gulf, the Bahrain attack caused damage but no injuries, and no US retaliation on Iranian soil was confirmed. The four axes therefore hold: kinetic 75, great-power 70, WMD 60, alliance 60.

The European pattern is the week's most consistent signal. Poland calls the missiles intentional, Denmark attributes an assassination plot to Russian intelligence and expelled an attaché, Estonia closes its road border, and Finland says the war is spilling over after a strike on a Russian ship in the Gulf of Finland. These are national responses, coordinated in solidarity statements, not an alliance rupture. At the same time Denmark ratified its Greenland deal with Washington, which removes a source of NATO friction.

What would move the score: a NATO shootdown or a casualty on allied territory; a US strike campaign on Iranian energy targets; deaths in a Gulf state from Iranian fire; or follow-up nuclear talks among the three powers, which would argue the other way.

cards.confidenceNote: Polish ministers and NATO quoted by BBC, The Guardian and Kyiv Independent (all read).
cards.title: Russian cruise missiles crash in Poland during mass attack on Ukraine
cards.summary: Two Kh-101 cruise missiles and a jet drone crashed in south-eastern Poland on 20 November, with no injuries, during an attack that killed at least eight people in Ukraine. Tusk called it intentional; NATO scrambled jets. Embassies in Kyiv were damaged, and a Russian ship burned in the Gulf of Finland.
cards.body:
Putin promised a painful answer to Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge, and the 20 November attack was one of the largest of the war by Zelensky's and Poland's description; Poland's operational commander put it at seven bombers, 26 Kalibr and 72 Kh-101 cruise missiles and more than 500 drones. Two Kh-101 missiles came down at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem and a jet drone at Molodycz, between 50 and 100 km from Nowa Deba, where an 11-nation coalition-of-the-willing exercise led by Britain and France was under way. Poland's defence minister called the timing not accidental, Tusk called it an intentional provocation, and Rutte agreed it did not look like a coincidence. A Swedish Gripen was cleared to engage but did not, which Poland attributed to weather.

This is the second Kh-101 to land in Poland this year; in July Warsaw said there was no reason to think Poland was the target. The change is in the stated intent, not the hardware. Poland's response so far is a request for AWACS and F-35 support, not an Article 4 call.

Pressure on Europe came on several tracks in the same days. Strikes damaged the Dutch and Austrian embassies in Kyiv, and France sought a Security Council meeting. Denmark attributed a foiled assassination plot to Russian intelligence and expelled its attaché. Estonia will close its road border from 1 December. Ukraine, for its part, hit the Sparta II, a cargo ship linked to Russia's defence ministry, in the eastern Gulf of Finland; it drifted into Finnish waters.

On the channels, Hungary lifted its block on the next EU accession step for Ukraine, the Abu Dhabi prisoner exchange has not started, and Russia says it will not negotiate under bridge strikes. The UN counted at least 372 civilians killed in October, nearly double a year earlier.

iran_lead.title: Attacks on Hormuz shipping reach ten tankers in a week
iran_lead.summary: UKMTO reported three tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz and a bulk carrier set ablaze off Khor Fakkan on 22 November; that brings reported tanker strikes since 16 November to 10, by gCaptain's count. The IMO counts 25 seafarers confirmed dead. Iran blacklisted 26 tugboats, and its Guard claimed two tankers hit mines on 25 November. No US strike on Iranian territory has been reported since 17 November.
facts: 22 Nov: UKMTO reports three tankers struck in Hormuz and a bulk carrier hit off Khor Fakkan.
24 Nov: Iran's strait authority blacklists 26 tugboats.
24 Nov: Swedish Club advises avoiding Hormuz; IMO counts 25 seafarers dead.
25 Nov: IRGC claims two tankers hit mines (unconfirmed).
iran_lead.changed: The attack rate on outbound tankers off Musandam rose to about ten in a week, all unattributed by UKMTO, while Iran widened its 'non-compliant' list from ships to the tugboats that serve them. The IMO raised its regional count to 141 incidents and 25 seafarer deaths, and The Swedish Club told members to avoid the strait unless passage is essential. Facilitated transits ran at about 26.5 a day on 15-18 November, by monitoring the club cited.
iran_lead.watch: Whether UKMTO or CENTCOM attributes the 22 November strikes; any US strike on Iranian territory or on a blockade runner; the IRGC mine claim's ships and position; insurers' war-risk terms; OPEC+ on 29 November.

brics_lead.title: North Korea expels Switzerland's envoy and orders its Pyongyang office shut
brics_lead.summary: North Korea ordered the closure of Switzerland's diplomatic office in Pyongyang on 25 November, declaring its head persona non grata and telling him to leave within 48 hours, a day after Kim Yo Jong's threat over Swiss sanctions on a camp linked to deported Ukrainian children. A US Army sergeant pleaded guilty on 24 November to passing HIMARS material to people connected to China.
brics_lead.changed: Pyongyang turned a Swiss sanctions listing tied to Russia's war into the loss of its newest Western diplomatic channel, a month after the Swiss foreign minister's visit. In the US, the Zhao plea adds a China case to the run of Russia-linked spying cases. No BRICS-bloc development was read in the window.
brics_lead.watch: Switzerland's response; Taiwan's 28 November local elections and any Chinese pressure around them; further Russian or Chinese flights near Korea and Japan; Beijing's reply to the Megaspeed listing.

lenses.oneline: A US Army sergeant pleaded guilty to passing HIMARS material to China-connected people; Taiwan votes on 28 November.

lenses.label: BRICS bloc
lenses.oneline: No BRICS-bloc development read in the window.

facts: 25 Nov: North Korea orders the Swiss office in Pyongyang closed; head declared persona non grata.
24 Nov: US Army Sgt Jian Zhao pleads guilty in a China defence-information case.
24 Nov: UK security agency warns firms of Russian sabotage.

ukraine_lead.title: Two Libyan soldiers die after Benghazi strike; Russia hits Ukraine's gas
ukraine_lead.summary: Two Libyan soldiers died of injuries from the Ukrainian-claimed drone strike on Russian ships at Benghazi, and France's foreign minister defended Ukraine's right to self-defence. Russian strikes overnight into 25 November halted a Naftogaz gas site and cut power in five regions. US negotiators have privately ruled out troops or bases in post-war Ukraine, the Kyiv Independent reports.
facts: 24 Nov: two Libyan soldiers die of injuries from the Benghazi strike.
25 Nov: Russian strikes halt a Naftogaz gas site; ZNPP loses outside power.
25 Nov: Kyiv Independent: US rules out troops and bases in post-war Ukraine.
24 Nov: Zelensky says 48 PURL-funded Patriots await Hegseth's sign-off.
ukraine_lead.changed: The Benghazi strike now has deaths on Libyan soil, and Haftar flew to Ankara two days later. Russia returned to Ukraine's gas production as winter sets in; the Zaporizhzhia plant lost outside power for the 17th time this year. On the diplomatic track, the US offer of an 'Article 5-like' guarantee comes without troops or bases, and Zelensky says 48 Patriot interceptors paid for by allies still await Hegseth's signature.
ukraine_lead.watch: Russia's reply to Benghazi; Estonia's 1 December border closure; the Abu Dhabi prisoner exchange; NATO foreign ministers on Poland's air-defence requests; Pentagon sign-off on the Patriots.
